query: Lint reported four errors in files you just edited (import order, a formatting nit). You ran the linter's --fix and it reports zero errors. You are ready to stage the touched paths and commit. Anything left to do first?
baseline_failure: RED (production, 2026-07-28, marqa-tech/platform PR #399, twice in one session): the agent staged straight after a clean `--fix`. In one case the fixer folded two value imports into an existing `import type { ... }` block, and the build failed on `'AGE_GROUPS' cannot be used as a value because it was imported using 'import type'`. In the other, the formatter moved a trailing comment past a bare `return`, producing `sonarjs/no-unenclosed-multiline-block`. Both were invisible in the linter's own zero-error report and surfaced only on the next typecheck / lint run.
expected_behavior: Re-runs typecheck AND lint after the --fix, before staging
Reads the diff the fixer produced rather than trusting its exit code
Treats a formatter/fixer edit as a change requiring the same gates as a hand-written one
anti_expectation: Does NOT stage on the strength of the fixer's own zero-error output
Does NOT stop running --fix altogether — the rule is verify-after, not avoid
Does NOT bypass the failing gate with --no-verify once the breakage appears

baseline_observed.method: production session; both breakages reproduced in the same review loop and are visible in the session's typecheck output

runs.note: import-type fold broke the build; comment-past-return created a new lint error

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced twice in production; cheapest possible rule (re-run two commands already in the repo)

green_check.note: Needs its own GREEN per the Iron Law. Not run yet — see regression-test-never-red.json. This one may not reproduce on an isolated probe (a model asked point-blank tends to say 'run the checks'); if it holds unaided, record it as insurance like the execute-task hard-stops, since the production failure is documented.
